import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 130

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/130](https://www.erdosproblems.com/130)
-/

namespace Erdos130

open EuclideanGeometry SimpleGraph

/--
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be an infinite set which contains no three points on a
line and no four points on a circle. Consider the graph with vertices the points
in $A$, where two vertices are joined by an edge if and only if they are an
integer distance apart. How large can the chromatic number and clique number of
this graph be? In particular, can the chromatic number be infinite?

The chromatic number can be infinite: there is an infinite general-position set
whose integer-distance graph admits no finite proper colouring. How large the
*clique* number can be is not addressed here.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-130/Research/Basic.lean"]
theorem erdos_130 :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∃ A : Set ℝ², A.Infinite ∧ InGeneralPosition A ∧
        (IntegerDistancePlaneGraph A).chromaticNumber = ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos130

reformulations.difference: The infinite chromatic number is expressed as equality to ⊤ in ℕ∞, rather than using a cardinal-valued chromatic number. Integer-distance edges are expressed using positive natural lengths.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib gives G.chromaticNumber ≠ ⊤ ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, G.Colorable n. Negating proves that equality to ⊤ means precisely that no finite proper colouring exists, which is the source's particular question. For distinct Euclidean points, an integer distance is strictly positive, so it is equivalently a positive natural distance. Both equivalences, and the resulting formulation that every finite colouring has a monochromatic integer-distance edge, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the sorry theorem.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/130 (read through https://r.jina.ai/http://www.erdosproblems.com/130, including the rendered HTML)
review.notes:
The sole declaration faithfully states the positive answer to the source's infinite-chromatic-number subquestion. The omitted clique-number question is explicitly excluded by the docstring. General position was checked against distinct triples and quadruples: T.ncard = 4 forces T to be finite, and four distinct cospherical planar points have a positive-radius circle. Boundary tests covered empty, singleton and finite vertex sets, loops, a 3–4–5 edge, and a nonintegral √2 distance.

The source still labels the broader Problem 130 OPEN; this alone does not make the chromatic-only theorem's solved tag stale. I checked the complete cited proof chain under local Lean 4.33.1, replacing two simp calls with rfl and Sum.inl_ne_inr for compatibility with its original Lean 4.31.0 toolchain, without changing any statement or definition. I also proved the translation from its coordinate model to the repository's definitions. The combined /workspace/review/verified.lean proves exactly the reviewed statement, and #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Thus the positive answer and formal_proof record are substantiated.
